title: Universalis Cosmographia (Waldseemüller World Map)
original_title: Universalis cosmographia secundum Ptholomaei traditionem et Americi Vespucii alioru[m]que lustrationes
description: First map to use the name 'America'; first to depict a separate Western Hemisphere and the Pacific as a distinct ocean.
historical_context: Produced in Saint-Dié (Lorraine) integrating data from Vespucci's 1501–1502 voyages.
institution_or_collection: Library of Congress, Geography and Map Division
license: No known copyright restrictions (LoC Geography & Map Division free-to-use statement)

title: Tabula Rogeriana
original_title: نزهة المشتاق في اختراق الآفاق (Nuzhat al-mushtāq fi'khtirāq al-āfāq)
description: World map made by al-Idrisi for King Roger II of Sicily; remained the most accurate world map for three centuries.
historical_context: Compiled at the Norman court of Palermo, integrating Arab geographic knowledge.
institution_or_collection: Bibliothèque nationale de France (MS Arabe 2221); copy by Konrad Miller (1929)
license: Public domain

title: Hereford Mappa Mundi
original_title: Hereford Mappa Mundi
description: Largest known medieval map of the world; depicts a T-O cosmology with Jerusalem at the center.
historical_context: Created at Hereford Cathedral; reflects medieval Christian geography.
license: Public domain

title: Ebstorf Map (reconstruction)
original_title: Ebstorfer Weltkarte
description: Largest medieval world map known; destroyed in WWII bombing of Hannover; reconstructions survive.
historical_context: Made in Ebstorf monastery; depicted Christ's body encompassing the world.
institution_or_collection: Original destroyed 1943; reconstructions in various German institutions
license: Public domain

title: Fra Mauro Map
original_title: Mappamondo di Fra Mauro
description: Considered the greatest memorial of medieval cartography; combines Marco Polo, Arab sources, and Portuguese explorations.
historical_context: Made in Venice by Camaldolese monk; oriented with south at top.
license: Public domain

title: Cantino Planisphere
original_title: Carta del Cantino
description: Earliest surviving map showing Portuguese discoveries in the east and west; first to show the Treaty of Tordesillas line.
historical_context: Smuggled out of Portugal by Alberto Cantino, agent of the Duke of Ferrara.
license: Public domain

title: Mercator World Map 1569
original_title: Nova et Aucta Orbis Terrae Descriptio ad Usum Navigantium Emendate Accommodata
description: First map to use the Mercator projection, designed for marine navigation with rhumb lines as straight segments.
historical_context: Revolutionary projection enabling consistent compass-bearing navigation; basis for modern nautical charts.
institution_or_collection: Various surviving copies (Basel University Library, etc.)
license: Public domain

title: Theatrum Orbis Terrarum (Ortelius) — World Map
original_title: Typus Orbis Terrarum
description: Frontispiece world map of the first modern atlas, the Theatrum Orbis Terrarum.
historical_context: Published in Antwerp; considered the first true atlas.
license: Public domain

title: Ptolemy World Map (15th c. reconstruction)
original_title: Cosmographia / Geographia
description: Reconstructed world map based on Claudius Ptolemy's Geographia; Ulm 1482 woodcut edition.
historical_context: Ptolemy's coordinates system was rediscovered in the Renaissance and shaped European cartography.
license: Public domain

title: Tabula Peutingeriana (Peutinger Map)
original_title: Tabula Peutingeriana
country_or_area: Europe, Mediterranean, Near East, Persia, India
description: Schematic itinerarium of the Roman cursus publicus; depicts road network from Britain to India.
historical_context: Medieval copy of a late-Roman administrative road map; 6.75 m long scroll.
license: Public domain

title: Catalan Atlas
original_title: Atles català
description: Majorcan illuminated nautical atlas combining portolan tradition with mappa mundi knowledge of Asia.
historical_context: Made in Palma for Charles V of France; landmark of Catalan-Jewish cartography.
license: Public domain

title: Juan de la Cosa World Map
original_title: Carta universal de Juan de la Cosa
description: Oldest surviving European map to show the Americas; depicts results of Columbus's first three voyages.
historical_context: Made by Columbus's pilot, who participated in the early voyages.

title: Codex Mendoza — frontispiece
original_title: Códice Mendoza

title: Carta Marina (Olaus Magnus)
original_title: Carta marina et descriptio septemtrionalium terrarum
